title: Preparing Predicted Grades Ahead of October…
summary: A practical fall-term plan for IB coordinators to prepare, moderate, approve, and submit defensible predicted grades before October deadlines.
body_markdown:
Preparing predicted grades ahead of October deadlines requires more than collecting numbers from subject teachers. An IB coordinator needs a shared evidence policy, moderation procedures, accurate application data, and enough time to resolve anomalies before school documents are submitted.


For the 2027 entry cycle, the main UCAS early deadline is **15 October 2026 at 18:00 UK time** for Oxford, Cambridge, and most medicine, dentistry, and veterinary medicine or science courses. US early deadlines vary by institution. Schools should work backward from each external deadline and freeze predictions several working days earlier.


### What an IB predicted grade represents


The[IB definition of a predicted grade](https://ibo.org/university-admission/discover-why-ib-students-succeed/ib-student-assessment/) is the teacher's prediction of the grade a candidate is expected to achieve, based on available evidence and knowledge of IB standards. Predictions should be as accurate as possible, without systematic over-prediction or under-prediction.


Diploma Programme subjects use the **1-7 scale** . Schools may also forecast **Theory of Knowledge** and **Extended Essay** outcomes to estimate core points and an overall Diploma total out of **45** .


A prediction is not:


- A reward for effort, attendance, or conduct
- A target chosen to satisfy university entry requirements
- The result of one unusually strong or weak assessment
- A guaranteed minimum result
- A grade awarded by the IB


University-facing forecasts and predictions submitted later through IB administrative processes may be produced at different times. They are distinct data snapshots, and additional evidence can legitimately change the later figure.


### Build the process backward from deadlines


The[UCAS dates and deadlines guidance](https://www.ucas.com/applying/applying-to-university/dates-and-deadlines-for-uni-applications) confirms the **15 October 2026** equal-consideration deadline for relevant 2027 entry applications. Because the reference must be completed before a linked application is sent, schools cannot leave predictions until deadline day.


Common App has no universal early deadline. Its[international applicant guidance](https://www.commonapp.org/static/84292aaf2c3c2ddb4425749e97dc9b00/Resource_FY_International_ENG_2025.06.24_1.pdf) explains that colleges set their own plans and dates.


Period Coordinator action Required output


Early September Confirm applicants, destinations, and courses Central deadline register


Mid-September Publish the evidence policy and cut-off Shared departmental instructions


Late September Collect subject and core forecasts Complete provisional record


Early October Moderate departments and borderline cases Approved predictions


5-7 working days before submission Freeze grades and check applications Locked master record


Before each deadline Approve references and submit documents Completed applications


The **internal freeze date** is a school decision, not an IB requirement. It should leave enough time to check qualification entries, subject levels, references, permissions, and portal status.


### Establish a defensible evidence policy


The IB does not prescribe one universal prediction formula. Departments should use evidence consistently and interpret it through current subject criteria and the official[DP grade descriptors](https://ibo.org/contentassets/0b0b7a097ca2498ea50a9e41d9e1d1cf/dp-grade-descriptors-en.pdf) .


Relevant evidence can include:


- Timed examinations or substantial paper sections
- End-of-DP1 and beginning-of-DP2 assessments
- Internal Assessment work completed by the cut-off
- Essays, practical work, oral tasks, and problem sets
- Recent performance trends
- Performance under independent conditions


No source is decisive by itself. A mock examination may reveal examination readiness but be affected by illness or incomplete syllabus coverage. An IA draft can demonstrate criterion-specific achievement, but it is not a final moderated mark.


Avoid imposing one percentage formula across every subject. Mathematics and Language A may require different evidence models, although both departments must explain how their forecasts match IB standards.


### Moderate for consistency, not uniformity


The coordinator should not replace subject-teacher judgement. Moderation tests whether that judgement is evidence-based, consistent, and accurately documented.


Departments should ask:


1. Is there enough recent evidence?
2. Was it interpreted against appropriate IB standards?
3. Are parallel classes applying comparable expectations?
4. Is the forecast credible alongside broader performance and historical patterns?


Historical predicted-versus-achieved data can reveal persistent optimism or caution, but coordinators should not apply an automatic adjustment to every student. Repeated over-prediction should lead to review of assessment design, marking, and standardization.


Prioritize borderline grades, unexplained jumps, identical predictions across a class, and inconsistencies between subjects and the total Diploma forecast. The[RevisionDojo guide to how IB predicted grades are set](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-ib-predicted-grades-are-set) can help schools explain this process to families.


### Define ownership and maintain an audit trail


A clear responsibility map prevents last-minute confusion. Subject teachers propose grades and retain evidence; heads of department standardize judgement; counselors check course choices and application requirements; the coordinator approves the process and controls the master record. Only named staff should be able to edit final figures.


Use a version-controlled spreadsheet or secure student information system that records the student, subject, level, proposed grade, approver, date, and reason for any change. Access should follow the school's data-protection rules because predictions are confidential educational records. Never circulate editable copies through informal messaging channels.


Schedule a short final sign-off meeting for unresolved cases. The purpose is not to negotiate grades, but to confirm that evidence has been reviewed and every change is authorized. After the freeze, edits should require a documented exception, such as a transcription error or previously unavailable assessment evidence. This audit trail allows the coordinator to answer later questions without relying on memory and makes annual evaluation of prediction accuracy more reliable.


### Separate judgement from application strategy


A predicted grade answers, “What is this student expected to achieve?” It should not answer, “What does this student need to apply?” Adjusting forecasts to match entry requirements undermines fairness and may expose students to unrealistic conditional offers.


Once predictions are approved, counselors can compare them with published requirements, typical competitive profiles, subject-specific HL conditions, and total Diploma offers. They can then help students balance aspirational, realistic, and safer choices without influencing academic judgement.


### Control application data carefully


UCAS guidance on[managing references and predicted grades](https://www.ucas.com/advisers/help-and-training/guides-resources-and-training/application-overview/our-adviser-portal/managing-references-and-predicted-grades-adviser-portal) states that predicted grades cannot be changed through UCAS after submission. Returning an application for amended education details may also remove predictions already entered.


Before approval, verify that:


- The qualification, examination session, subjects, and levels are correct
- Pending qualifications appear properly
- Portal grades match the locked school record
- The reference is complete and consistent
- A second authorized staff member has checked the application


For US applications, verify each college's requirements for transcripts, counselor recommendations, School Reports, and midyear reports. Common App's[school-form guidance](https://recsupport.commonapp.org/recommendersupport/s/article/What-are-the-deadlines-for-submission-of-the-school-forms) advises submitting documents by the institution's listed deadline.


### Manage reviews and digital evidence


Publish the review procedure before releasing predictions. A student should first ask the teacher to explain the evidence, followed where necessary by departmental review and coordinator consideration of procedural concerns. Changes should correct errors or account for material academic evidence, not respond to university ambitions or parental pressure.


The[RevisionDojo guide to parent conversations](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-coordinators-predicted-grades-parent-guide) provides a framework for keeping discussions evidence-focused. Decisions and rationales should be recorded consistently.


Digital practice can support improvement before the evidence cut-off, but platform scores are not official predictions.[RevisionDojo Mock Exams](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) , Questionbank, IA Feedback, and Jojo AI can help students identify weaknesses, while teachers retain responsibility for authentic assessment and professional judgement. Families may also benefit from the[predicted-grade submission timeline guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/when-are-ib-predicted-grades-submitted-to-universities-what-every-student-needs-to-know) , which distinguishes university, school, and IB timelines.


### Conclusion


Preparing predicted grades ahead of October deadlines is an academic quality-assurance task. A backward-planned calendar, defensible evidence policy, documented moderation, controlled review process, and second-person application check protect students and the school. RevisionDojo can support evidence-building through Questionbank, Mock Exams, IA Feedback, and Jojo AI, while the school remains responsible for every official prediction.
